You are a senior full-stack web developer and UI/UX designer.
Your task is to build a complete, professional, conversion-focused FREELANCE WEBSITE DEVELOPER PORTFOLIO WEBSITE.

This project must be treated as a real client-ready commercial website, not a demo.

🚫 STRICT RULES (VERY IMPORTANT)

Use HTML, CSS, JavaScript ONLY



✅ This is a professional WEBSITE

Code must be clean, structured, scalable & production-ready

📦 CODE OUTPUT HANDLING (MANDATORY)

If the full project code is too large:

PART 1

Write maximum possible complete code

Include full file structures & logic

End at a clean stopping point

Clearly mention:
“END OF PART 1 – Say ‘Continue from last’ to proceed”

PART 2 (and PART 3 if needed)

Continue exactly from where last part ended

❌ Do NOT rewrite previous code

❌ Do NOT skip any feature

Never shorten or remove features to save space.

🌐 WEBSITE PURPOSE

Showcase website development services

Convert visitors into WhatsApp / Call / Enquiry leads

Clearly explain 3 pricing plans

Build trust for a new freelance developer

Make site future-ready for agency growth

🎯 TARGET AUDIENCE

creators

Doctors

Consultants

Small businesses

Startups

Local service providers

🧱 REQUIRED PAGES (MIN 10)

Create clean, SEO-friendly pages:

Home

About Developer

Services

Portfolio / Sample Work

Pricing Plans

Plan Comparison

Testimonials

FAQ

Contact

Privacy Policy

Terms & Conditions

💰 PRICING PLANS (VERY IMPORTANT)

Create 3 pricing cards with feature scaling.

🟢 BASIC PLAN – ₹2,999

3–4 pages

Responsive design

Simple custom UI

WhatsApp & contact form

Basic SEO structure

🔵 STANDARD PLAN – ₹5,999

8–10 professional pages

Custom design (Not WordPress theme)

Mobile & desktop responsive

Easy-to-use admin panel (CMS)

WhatsApp, Call & Enquiry integration

SEO-ready structure

Fast loading & secure website

Delivery in 7–10 working days

No hidden charges

🔴 PREMIUM PLAN – ₹9999

30 pages

Advanced CMS controls

Performance optimization & caching

Enhanced security best practices

Portfolio & testimonials management

Priority support & delivery

🎨 UI / UX DESIGN RULES

Professional corporate website look

Top navigation bar only (❌ NO bottom navigation)

Clean typography & spacing

Card-based sections

Smooth hover & scroll animations

Strong CTA buttons:

“Get Quote”

“WhatsApp Now”

Sticky header allowed

Floating WhatsApp button allowed

🧰 TECHNICAL FEATURES (MANDATORY)

Modular JavaScript architecture

supabase DB

Form validation (client side)

SEO-friendly semantic HTML

Fast loading optimization

Secure input handling

PWA support (optional but structured)

Offline caching (where relevant)

Hosting ready for InfinityFree / shared hosting

🧠 CMS / ADMIN PANEL REQUIREMENTS

Simple admin login system

Add / edit / delete pages

Update text, pricing & sections

Store data locally (supabase)

Clean admin UI (basic but usable)

📈 BUSINESS & CONVERSION OPTIMIZATION

Pricing comparison table

Highlight value over price

Trust sections (why choose me)

Testimonial placeholders

Upsell-ready layout (SEO, maintenance, hosting)

Lead-focused layout on every page

🛡 QUALITY EXPECTATIONS

Code must be readable & commented

Logical folder structure

Reusable CSS & JS components

No hard-coded messy styles

Future-scalable architecture

🛑 FINAL CHECK BEFORE OUTPUT

Before finishing:

Confirm all pricing plans are implemented

Confirm feature scaling is correct

Confirm no bottom navigation exists

Confirm website look (not app-like)

Confirm code split rules are followed

**Defining the Portfolio Goals**

I'm now zeroing in on defining the precise goals for this Freelance Website Developer Portfolio. My focus is on ensuring it's comprehensive, professional, and laser-focused on conversions, keeping in mind the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript constraint. I'm exploring various portfolio website structures to determine the most effective layout for showcasing skills and attracting clients.


**Resolving System Conflicts**

I'm navigating the system's request for React, TypeScript, and Tailwind, despite the user's initial mention of HTML/CSS/JavaScript. My approach is to ensure the functional requirements are met, like the user's specific pages and Supabase integration, within the requested tech stack. I'm choosing the SPA architecture with React as the framework.


**Structuring the Web Pages**

I'm now determining the structure of the pages. I plan to incorporate "About," "Services," "Portfolio," and "Pricing" with three distinct plans, "Testimonials," "FAQ," "Contact," "Privacy Policy," "Terms & Conditions," and an implied "Admin Dashboard."

**Defining the Tech Stack**

I've selected the core tech stack: React with a Vite-like structure, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Supabase. I'm focusing on creating `supabaseClient.ts` and associated service functions. I can provide the basic structure with mock Supabase calls or local storage, ready for a real DB connection if keys are provided.


**Implementing Mock Data**

I'm making the site immediately runnable by integrating a mock toggle or fallback mechanism. Focusing on UI/UX, I've outlined a professional corporate aesthetic with top navigation, a floating WhatsApp button, and strong CTAs, ensuring responsiveness with a mobile-first approach. Pricing plans are now defined, and the Admin Panel will feature simulated content editing.


**Developing the Core Data**

I'm now zeroing in on data management within the single-page application (SPA) architecture. My work focuses on creating `supabase.ts` for client setup, and `dataService.ts` for data fetching. For the "Admin Panel", the plan is to use a client-side interface with simulated content editing via Context or Store for immediate session changes. I'm taking a step-by-step approach starting with setup, core UI components, and defining essential data.


**Outlining Component Structure**

I'm now drafting the content flow, starting with the header, hero section, services breakdown, and the three-tiered pricing plans as requested. I'll implement a trust section with testimonials and "Why Me?" copy. For the Supabase integration, I will provide the setup code, but I'll wrap the calls in a try/catch or use a "Mock Service" so that users can run the app without crashing if the keys are missing.
I have also created an initial file list, including metadata, the HTML entry, the main TypeScript application file and TypeScript types, key constants, Supabase service, and fundamental components.


**Organizing the Components**

I'm now consolidating components and carefully structuring the "Pages" to manage file count. I'm focusing on defining pricing details: Basic at ₹2,999, Standard at ₹5,999, and Premium at ₹9,999, with features listed for each plan. I'm interpreting "JavaScript architecture" as React due to the instructions. I will use a Context to simulate CMS functionality, with the admin panel updating this context. I will include Tailwind via CDN, and I'm prepared to start coding.

Yahan bataya gaya hai ki ye kaise kaam karta hai:

### 1. Supabase Edge Functions (Sabse Best Tareeka)
Supabase mein **"Edge Functions"** hote hain. Ye chhote server-side scripts hote hain jo Supabase par hi host hote hain. Aap ek function bana sakte hain jo tab trigger hoga jab bhi koi user inquiry table mein naya data insert karega.

### 2. Email Service Provider (ESP)
Directly database se email nahi jata, uske liye aapko ek email provider use karna padega (jaise **Resend**, **SendGrid**, ya **Mailgun**).
*   **Process:** Supabase (DB Insert) -> Edge Function Trigger -> Email Service (Resend) -> Aapka Mail Inbox.

### 3. Kya aapko server launch karna padega?
**Nahi.** Supabase ek "Backend-as-a-Service" hai. Edge functions "Serverless" hote hain, iska matlab hai ki infrastructure Supabase khud handle karta hai. Aapko bas code wahan deploy karna hota hai.

### 4. Kya main ye kar sakta hoon?

1.  Supabase dashboard mein ek **Database Webhook** ya **Edge Function** banana hoga.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.inquiries (

);

);

    name text not null,
    role text,

);

);

CREATE POLICY "Enable select for authenticated users only" ON public.inquiries FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true);
